near_miss.why_not: ON law formula 'forfeits property and peace' (firirgort fe ok friði) vs Vedic 'dear to cattle'; different syntax and sense, shared roots only.

near_miss.lead: faður frændr ok moður frændr ~ mātṛ pitṛ lists
near_miss.why_not: Kin-term enumerations: generic and found everywhere; the ON is a legal clause about guardianship by paternal and maternal kin, the MBh lines laments. No shared collocation.

near_miss.lead: sun and moon pair: Sól ... mána ... vissi ~ ni vidjela sunca ni mjeseca
near_miss.why_not: Cognate pair sól/sunce, máni/mjesec, but the Serbian is an idiom for confinement (has not seen sun nor moon), with the sun as object; in Vsp 5 the sun is the subject and does not know her halls. Sun+moon merism is universal. Better partner is OHG Wessobrunn (see search lead for BS-90cc0).

near_miss.lead: daughter in father's/brother's house: dotter er legen j faður garde eða brodor ~ sā mātuḥ badhyatām gṛhe atha u bhrātuḥ atha u pituḥ
near_miss.why_not: Surface match (daughter + house of father/brother) but ON 'legin' means seduced (the clause disinherits a daughter seduced in her father's house; cf. MLL 35r:25 'ef dóttir er legin í fǫðurgarði'), while AVŚ 1.14 is a spell to keep a girl unmarried at home. Different situations; garðr ~ gṛha cognacy not secure.

near_miss.lead: crowing cock: hani (< *kan- 'singer') gól/gelr ~ Lat. aves canere, merula cantat
near_miss.why_not: The *kan- root sits in the ON noun hani, not the verb (gala); the Latin has canere of birds generally. A lexical fact, not a shared phrase; Latin partners are not about cocks.

near_miss.lead: dream vision: um nottena er hann var i sœmn komenn þa sa hann ~ hac nocte in somnis visus sum viderier (night + sleep loc. + see; svefn ~ somnus, nátt ~ nox)
near_miss.why_not: Close surface match with two cognates, but the ON is Olaf hagiography written under Latin models (in somnis vidit, nocte quadam), so the wording is likely calqued, not inherited; dream-report language is also generic. The idiomatic native ON is dreyma. Not defensible as inherited.

near_miss.lead: af allum hug oc hiarta ~ hṛdi ... manasā (heart and mind)
near_miss.why_not: Heart+mind pair with hiarta ~ hṛd cognate, hugr renewing manas; but the ON is Christian hagiography echoing Biblical 'ex toto corde', and the AVP line is not a prayer formula 'with all heart and mind'. Biblical source is likelier; heart/mind pairing is generic.

near_miss.lead: end-time breakdown of kinship: Bræðr munu berjaz ... mun engi maðr öðrum þyrma ~ брат брата не съжаляшеть ся ни отьць сынови ни мати дъчери (bróðir ~ bratъ, polyptoton in the ORV)
near_miss.why_not: Same topos with cognate 'brother', but the Novgorod famine entry plainly echoes Mark 13:12 / Micah 7:6, and Vsp 45 may itself draw on Christian apocalyptic; no shared syntax beyond the kin term. Hesiod WD 182-184 (kasignētos, renewed) is the better non-Biblical partner (search lead).
ON alliterative doublet in a chains-loosed miracle (Acts 12 model); MBh only has baddhvā 'having bound'. No shared figure.

near_miss.lead: Munu ósánir akrar vaxa (unsown fields will grow)
near_miss.why_not: RV/AV partners (barhis, ukṣ-) unrelated. Golden-age 'unsown growth' parallels exist outside the slab (search lead), but with renewed verbs.

near_miss.lead: negative cosmogony: var-a sandr né sær ... jörð fannz æva ne upphiminn
near_miss.why_not: MBh partner is irrelevant; the real partners (OHG Wessobrunn, RV 10.129) are outside the slab: see search lead.
The Indic partners are colour lists (nīla piśaṅga lohita), not 'redden with blood'. Real partner is Homeric, outside the slab: see search lead.

search_lead.cognate: ON rjóða (rýðr) ~ Gk ἐρυθαίνω, both *h₁rewdʰ- 'redden'; instrumental 'blood' renewed (dreyri/blóð ~ αἷμα); ON adds figura etymologica rýðr ... rauðum
search_lead.argument: Same verb-root + instrumental 'blood' + a place as subject/object (gods' seats; earth, river water) in battle/slaughter contexts. ON skaldic verse (Sigvatr/Óttarr quoted in the Olaf legend) uses rjóða + blóð as a native formula, so not a Latinism. The collocation is natural, hence medium-low weight, but the verb root is shared and the construction identical.

words: noh sunna ni scein noh mano ni-liuhta

search_lead.cognate: jǫrð ~ OHG ero, upphiminn ~ ufhimil (exact compound), negated past 'be' (var-a ~ ni uuas, OHG and ON from *h₂wes-; Ved. ná āsīt from *h₁es-, renewal); sun/moon clause in Vsp 5 ~ Wessobrunn 'noh sunna ni scein noh mano ni liuhta'
search_lead.argument: Negative cosmogony 'there was neither earth nor up-heaven' with an identical compound in ON and OHG, and the same 'not was X nor Y' frame in RV 10.129 (no air, no sky beyond; no sign of night or day). Germanic pair is well known; the Vedic leg is a structural parallel with renewed lexemes, and Near Eastern and Christian negative cosmogonies (Gen 2:5; Wessobrunn is a Christian prayer) weaken the inheritance case.

search_lead.cognate: privative ó- ~ ἀ- ~ a- (*n̥-) + 'sown/ploughed' participle (renewed: sá- vs σπείρω; kṛṣ-) + 'grow' (vaxa vs φύομαι, renewed)
search_lead.argument: Golden-age motif 'fields grow unsown' in Vsp 62 (renewed world), Od. 9.109 (Cyclopes) and Ved. akṛṣṭapacya- 'ripening unploughed'. Only the privative is cognate; motif rather than phrase.

search_lead.cognate: none exact: bróðir renewed by κασίγνητος; future of 'be' + kin term
search_lead.argument: Breakdown of kin loyalty as a sign of the last, worst age (Vsp 45 skeggǫld skálmǫld ~ Hesiod's iron age). Motif-level only; Christian apocalyptic (Mark 13:12) is a competing source for Vsp.

error.evidence: ON veita 'grant' is not the causative of *weyd-; usually connected with *weyh₁- (Skt. véti, Lat. invītus). Same error in DG-8-OHleg 0107:15 (w7/8) væittu tiðir.
kalla is unrelated to *ǵerh₂- 'grow old'; it belongs with OCS glasъ / glagolъ (*gol-s-).
Proper name mapped as a common noun.

note: Second reading of 17 flagged bundles. No claims: best leads (dream-vision night+sleep+see, kin-breakdown Vsp 45 ~ Novgorod famine) are probably Latin/Biblical in origin. Search leads: rjóða + blood ~ Il. ἐρυθαίνετο αἵματι; Vsp 3 ~ Wessobrunn/RV 10.129; unsown fields; Hesiod WD 184.
